title: A Letter for the Alibi
premise: Estate lawyer Isandro Sandoval is summoned to read the will of Marisol Vega, a woman declared legally dead seven years ago—yet the will is dated three years after her disappearance. Following the document's trail, Isandro finds Marisol's hidden diary, whose entries continue past the date she vanished, suggesting she lived in hiding until very recently—and may still be alive. As Isandro traces the diary's coded references through the coastal town of Punta Clara, she uncovers a found family Marisol built in the shadows, and a powerful family whose inheritance depended on her staying dead. When the diary's final entry names Isandro herself, she realizes she was chosen as reader, not by accident but by design. In the end, Isandro must choose between the letter of the law that made her career and the living woman it would erase—closing the case not with a death certificate, but with Marisol's chosen rebirth.
about_author: Noor Blackwood is the pen name of a former legal archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed estates and the strange paper trails people leave behind. They write mysteries about documents that outlive their owners, from a house full of filing cabinets by the sea.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Isandro Sandoval, meticulous and guarded, is hired to execute the estate of Marisol Vega—legally dead for seven years. The will is dated three years after her disappearance, notarized with an authentic seal. Isandro's professional pride demands she find the flaw. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: cold curiosity masking an old wound about cases that refuse to close.

chapters.title: Punta Clara's Long Memory
chapters.summary: Arriving in the fog-bound coastal town, Isandro interviews the executor's named witnesses: a diner owner, a retired harbor clerk, a priest who all claim to barely remember Marisol. Their denials are too synchronized. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: unease—the town is a closed mouth.

chapters.title: The Diary's Impossible Dates
chapters.summary: Following the will's instructions to a rented boathouse, Isandro finds Marisol's diary. Entries continue past the official date of death, growing more coded, until the last page: 'Give it to the lawyer who never loses.' POV: Isandro, with diary excerpts in Marisol's voice. Emotional beat: the thrill of a live case turning to dread.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Marisol's early diary voice: her life before disappearance, her engagement to Emilio Ferrer of the shipping Ferrers, and the night she learned what marrying into that family would cost her. POV: Marisol (diary). Emotional beat: love curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Ferrer Inheritance
chapters.summary: Isandro digs into probate records: Marisol's 'death' unlocked a trust that saved the Ferrer shipping empire. Patriarch Aurelio Ferrer now runs for governor. Isandro requests an interview and is warned off—politely, then not. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the first taste of real danger.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Diner
chapters.summary: Diner owner Rosa Reyes, the weakest liar of the three witnesses, slips: she mentions a dish only Marisol ever ordered. Isandro returns at closing; Rosa admits Marisol lived hidden in town for two years, protected by a small circle. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: first ally, first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Rosa introduces Isandro to the circle: harbor clerk Teo, nurse Camille, and teenage Lucía, whom Marisol tutored in secret. Each holds one piece of Marisol's hidden life and one reason to distrust lawyers. POV: Isandro, alternating with Lucía's wary observations. Emotional beat: guarded warmth—Isandro feels the pull of belonging she's always refused.

chapters.title: Someone Else Is Reading
chapters.summary: The boathouse is searched; pages of the diary are missing. Isandro realizes a second party has the will's existence and is working backward to the circle. She sets a trap with a false diary location. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: Emilio Ferrer, Widower
chapters.summary: Emilio grants Isandro an interview—grieving, charming, and precise about dates he should have no reason to know. He offers to buy the estate's administration outright. Isandro declines and notices his cufflink matches a button found in the boathouse. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: attraction to a suspect, and self-disgust at it.

chapters.title: The Night Boat
chapters.summary: Teo's memory: the night Marisol 'drowned,' a second boat left the harbor, and Teo helped row it—her escape, arranged by someone inside the Ferrer house. The diary hints who: initials A.V. POV: Teo's confession to Isandro. Emotional beat: loyalty tested across seven years.

chapters.title: A.V.
chapters.summary: Isandro traces A.V. to Ana Vega, Marisol's sister, who inherited everything and has quietly funneled money offshore ever since. Ana denies everything—until Isandro shows her the diary's post-death entries and Ana's face collapses. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: betrayal inside the one family Marisol trusted.

chapters.title: What the Dead Owe the Living
chapters.summary: Ana confesses: Marisol's escape was real, but three years ago Ana sold information about her sister's location to the Ferrers to cover her own debts. She doesn't know if Marisol fled again or was found. POV: Ana, framed by Isandro's interrogation. Emotional beat: guilt as a living thing.

chapters.title: The Governor's Campaign
chapters.summary: Aurelio Ferrer's gubernatorial launch dominates Punta Clara; his speech invokes his lost future daughter-in-law. Isandro attends and is recognized by his security chief—the same man who searched the boathouse. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the case and the town's future colliding.

chapters.title: Lucía's Secret
chapters.summary: Lucía, frightened, reveals Marisol taught her a cipher and left her a sealed letter 'for when the lawyer asks.' Inside: coordinates to a mainland safe deposit box. Lucía begs Isandro not to make her a witness. POV: Lucía. Emotional beat: a child carrying an adult's burden.

chapters.title: Safe Deposit
chapters.summary: In the box: a second identity, cash, and photographs proving Aurelio Ferrer ordered surveillance on Marisol for years—and a recent photo, dated eight months ago, of a woman who might be her, alive. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: hope arriving as evidence.

chapters.title: Followed
chapters.summary: Isandro is tailed back to Punta Clara and narrowly loses the car on the coast road. The circle debates scattering; Rosa refuses to abandon the diner. Isandro realizes protecting them means finishing fast. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: duty transforming into devotion.

chapters.title: The Cipher's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Decoding the diary's final pages with Lucía's help, Isandro finds Marisol's plan: she knew Ana betrayed her, staged her own second disappearance, and left the will as a time capsule—meant to surface only when the Ferrers felt safe. The addressee clause names Isandro because Marisol researched her: the lawyer who never abandons a case. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: being seen, utterly, by a stranger.

chapters.title: Emilio's Confession
chapters.summary: Isandro confronts Emilio with the surveillance photos. He breaks: he never stopped loving her, discovered his father's hunt, and warned Marisol before the second disappearance. He agrees to testify—but that night, his car goes off the same coast road. POV: Emilio's recorded statement, then Isandro at the crash scene. Emotional beat: the cost of truth, exacted immediately.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Testimony
chapters.summary: Emilio survives, barely, and from his hospital bed signs a sworn statement. Aurelio's men move on the circle; Rosa is detained on fabricated charges. Isandro has forty-eight hours before the estate is seized and the diary ruled inadmissible. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Isandro forces an emergency probate hearing, arguing the will's validity proves Marisol lived past her declared death—making the Ferrer trust fraudulent. Aurelio's counsel attacks; the notary who sealed the will is produced: Camille's aunt, Marisol's quiet accomplice. POV: Isandro, in the courtroom where she's always been safest. Emotional beat: her armor finally serving something larger than herself.

chapters.title: Marisol Vega, Present
chapters.summary: At the hearing's climax, a woman in a headscarf rises from the gallery and identifies herself. Marisol, alive, chooses to end her invisibility to bury Aurelio's candidacy and free her circle. Aurelio is arrested for conspiracy; Ana surrenders to Isandro's negotiated plea. POV: Marisol, then Isandro. Emotional beat: love and identity reclaimed in public light.

chapters.title: A Letter for the Alibi
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Isandro closes the file and stays for Rosa's Sunday dinner—the circle adopting her whether she consents or not. Marisol gives her the diary's true last page: a thank-you letter, written for the alibi of a life that never existed, and the beginning of one that finally does. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the case closed, the family open.
